title: Add a Local tab for self-hosted model usage
head: 792b50f0636c
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Open #12803 silently defeats the stacked Codex provider guard when merged
leads.consequence: #12803 adds a pre-JSON gate admitting only token_count and turn_context, before this PR's session_meta.model_provider check. Merged Codex counts Ollama and OpenRouter rollouts as subscription usage again; Ollama rollouts also land on Local, so counts overlap. The Codex tab reports extra tokens even after --force. Current head tests pass individually but both local and Codex scanner tests fail against merged Codex code. Restore session_meta as an accepted prefilter line before merging both PRs.
leads.triage: verified directly (triage/codex.merged three-way merge) and by Opus self-check run df38baf9; published

leads.summary: Immutable SQLite reader misses committed OpenCode messages while OpenCode is running
leads.consequence: OpenCode enables WAL; immutable=1 tells SQLite not to inspect the -wal sidecar. A committed local-model message not checkpointed into the main database yields a successful empty Local record, and the empty result is cached (up to 20 seconds normally, 15 minutes on --limits-only). While OpenCode remains active the next scan can miss the same usage again. Use an ordinary read-only connection and query_only like the Codex collector.
leads.triage: already in Opus final F1; published

leads.summary: Local scanner ignores OpenCode v2 session_message rows
leads.consequence: The query only reads classic message. OpenCode also writes assistant records to session_message; a user whose local-model activity is all in that table gets an empty Local tab, despite a successful, cached scan. Add a v2 reader using that table's type and nested provider/model shape, without double counting classic rows.
leads.triage: Opus follow-up 1: real but shared with Codex/Claude collectors on base; not published

leads.summary: Pi's built-in llama.cpp provider is absent from Local's fallback set
leads.consequence: A Pi session using the shipped /llama llama.cpp integration writes provider llama.cpp, not llama-cpp or llamacpp. With no Codex provider of that name and no explicit local.json override, every such assistant message is silently skipped and its Local tab remains empty. Add the exact ID llama.cpp, plus a Pi fixture.
leads.triage: already in Opus final F2; published

leads.summary: Pi and OMP profile, explicit and XDG session roots are invisible
leads.consequence: Only ~/.pi/agent/sessions and ~/.omp/agent/sessions are walked. Sessions created with OMP --profile, OMP XDG_DATA_HOME storage, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR or Pi's session directory override can live outside these roots. Even a fully populated local-model profile reports zero on this collector; #9546 adds profile scanning to Codex and Claude, but not Local. Enumerate supported roots and use their resulting paths when forming the cache key.
leads.triage: dropped: same hardcoded roots in Codex and Claude collectors

leads.summary: Known runtime ID wins even when its configured endpoint is remote
leads.consequence: The collector accepts ollama or lmstudio before checking Codex config.toml's actual base_url. Those runtime providers can be redirected, including via Codex's CODEX_OSS_BASE_URL. A session billed by a remote endpoint is displayed as work on hardware the user owns. Check an available URL first; use the known-ID fallback only when no endpoint is known. Separately document that a DNS name is only parsed, not resolved, if runtime DNS resolution is intentionally omitted.
leads.triage: already in Opus F6; published as docs bullet

leads.summary: Configured mixed-case OpenCode provider IDs are filtered out in SQL
leads.consequence: User configuration lowercases providers, and provider_is_local lowercases incoming IDs, but SQL compares the original JSON providerID with lowercase candidates using case-sensitive IN. An OpenCode provider MyGateway named in local.json is skipped, even though the matching Python predicate would accept it. Normalize the SQL expression to match the Python classifier or preserve and include original spellings.
leads.triage: merged with Opus F7 nit; not published

leads.summary: Related all-provider Pi/OpenCode collectors would count the same Local rows
leads.consequence: Both open PRs are diverged, not stacked. #10330 removes Pi from the subscription collectors but adds a Pi tab deliberately counting every Pi/OMP backend; Local still counts local Pi/OMP, so each self-hosted Pi turn appears in both Pi and Local. #12635 adds an OpenCode tab deliberately counting every database assistant; Local still counts local OpenCode. This may be intended as two views of the same activity, but needs explicit coordination before either lands, especially if users sum tab totals. The README and manifest edits conflict in both integrations.
leads.triage: already in Opus interactions; published as one sentence

leads.summary: Pi IDs are deduplicated globally, but the producer only ensures file-local uniqueness
leads.consequence: Pi generates an eight-hex-character ID checked only against entries in the current session. Separate sessions (or Pi versus OMP) can share one ID with different model and usage; whichever is visited second loses its entire response in Local. Retain deduplication for genuinely copied fork entries, but scope it to session lineage or include a fingerprint and path instead of globally equating short IDs.

leads.summary: The shipped AI manual and settings example omit the newly supported Local provider
leads.consequence: The user-facing provider list still says only Claude Code, Codex and Fireworks are supported. The README example presented as the complete providers object lists those three but not local; users copying it will still have Local enabled by implicit default and cannot tell how to disable it. Add Local to the list and to the enable/disable example (or explicitly explain implicit enablement).
leads.triage: manual part in Opus F6, published; settings example is an illustrative subset, dropped

leads.summary: New Local scanner test passes when Pi/OMP scanning is entirely removed
leads.consequence: The changed test claims Local counts Pi, yet creates no Pi/OMP transcript. Removing scan.scan_pi() makes all 11 of its assertions pass. A Pi assistant fixture with a self-hosted provider, preferably the real llama.cpp ID, and an assertion for its token count would catch this regression.
leads.triage: already in Opus F5; published in optional test note

leads.summary: User overrides can reclassify subscription-owned provider IDs across tools
leads.consequence: An OpenCode user may configure the built-in provider ID openai with a LAN baseURL, then add openai to local.json so that Local will include its OpenCode rows. Because the override is global, the same Local run also includes native Codex rollouts tagged openai, and the stacked Codex collector includes them too. Both collectors also accept OpenCode providerID openai. A per-source override or explicit exclusion of subscription IDs is needed to retain the advertised disjointness.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** four behaviours do not match the description: turns still in opencode's WAL, pi on `llama.cpp`, a partition gap with the Codex collector, and one opencode row with an unexpected shape. Each has a small fix. A related open PR, #12803, also affects the #12032 change. Details follow, checked at `792b50f0`.

**Verified:** the Local collector is wired in correctly.
- `omarchy-agent-usage-update` picks the new collector up by glob. In the panel, the tab stays hidden with no data, the limits section and its separator are hidden when `limits` is empty, and the hero shows "Self-hosted". The panel and sync aggregation were checked by reading the code (`Main.qml`, `Panel.qml`), not by rendering.
- The six agent-usage test files pass at this head with 77 assertions, as stated.
- #12032's new Codex test fails against the base Codex collector ("Codex collector counts only subscription-backed native sessions") and passes with the change.
- The head merges cleanly with the current `quattro` tip.

### opencode rows still in the WAL are not counted

`bin/omarchy-agent-usage-local:315` opens the database with `?mode=ro&immutable=1`. opencode runs its database in WAL mode (opencode v1.18.32, `packages/core/src/database/database.ts:27`). With `immutable=1`, SQLite skips locking and change detection and does not read the WAL, so rows committed since the last checkpoint are invisible. The Codex and Claude collectors open the same file with `db.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro"` and `timeout=2`.

Synthetic WAL-mode database, writer connection still open, rows committed but not checkpointed:

```text
                           Local collector   Codex collector
ollama row (100 tokens)          0                 -
openai row (50 tokens)           -                 50
after wal_checkpoint             100               -
```

**Impact:** while opencode is running, the Local tab misses its newest turns. The test builds its database with the default rollback journal, so it cannot catch this. The size of the lag on a live opencode was not measured.

**Suggested change:** `sqlite3.connect(db.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True, timeout=2)`, as the sibling collectors do. With only that line changed, the same fixture reports 100.

### pi's `llama.cpp` provider is not recognised

`KNOWN_LOCAL_PROVIDERS` has `llama-cpp` and `llamacpp`, but pi's built-in llama.cpp provider records the id `llama.cpp` (pi v0.87.1, `packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/provider.ts:19`). opencode's provider docs use the same id in their llama-server example. pi and opencode sessions record only the provider id, so this list, `local.json` and any same-named Codex `model_providers` entry are the only ways their turns get classified.

**Impact:** "pi on llama.cpp", named in the docstring and README as an example, is not counted. A synthetic pi session with a `llama.cpp` assistant message (111 tokens) and an `ollama` one (22) reports 22.

**Suggested change:** add `llama.cpp` to the list. Longer term, pi's `models.json` (`providers.<id>.baseUrl`, for custom providers) and opencode's config (`provider.<id>.options.baseURL`) do record endpoints, so reading them would let most pi and opencode providers be classified by URL, as the README describes. pi's built-in llama.cpp provider keeps its URL elsewhere, so its id still needs to be listed.

### Rollouts without a readable `session_meta` are counted by both tabs

With a `session_meta`, the two collectors decide in opposite directions; without one, both count the rollout:

```text
rollout first line                Codex (#12032)    Local
session_meta, provider openai     counts            skips
session_meta, local provider      skips             counts
no session_meta / unreadable      counts            counts   <- both
```

#12032's own "legacy" fixture has this shape. Recreated, Codex counts `gpt-legacy` 40 and Local also counts `gpt-legacy` 40. The partition test compares only model names across rollouts that all have a `session_meta`, and does not compare token sums, so it passes.

**Impact:** limited in practice. Current Codex writes `session_meta` first when it creates a rollout, so this takes a missing or truncated first line. It is still the case the description says is asserted.

**Suggested change:** in `_scan_codex_file`, count `token_count` lines only after a local `session_meta` has been seen. That variant passes the PR's Local test (11/11) and removes the overlap in the same probe.

### One opencode row with an unexpected shape stops the rest of the opencode scan

In `scan_opencode`, the per-row `try` covers only `json.loads`. The `.get` calls on `tokens`, `cache` and `time` (`:346-348`) are outside it, so a row that is valid JSON with an unexpected shape (for example `"cache": 7`) raises into the outer handler, which marks the scan incomplete and returns. With rows of 10 tokens, that shape, and 1000 tokens, Local reports 10 and writes no cache. The Codex collector keeps these shape checks inside its per-row `try`.

**Impact:** the Local tab undercounts every opencode row after the first one with that shape. Because an incomplete scan is not cached, every run stops at the same row.

**Suggested change:** move the token and time extraction inside the per-row `try`.

### Interaction with open #12803

#12803 adds a prefilter to the Codex collector that skips any line without `"token_count"` or `"turn_context"` before JSON parsing. The collector file merges with this PR's Codex change without a conflict (the Codex scanner test file conflicts, since both PRs append to it). A `session_meta` line contains neither string, so #12032's provider check is never reached:

```python
for raw in handle:
  if '"token_count"' not in raw and '"turn_context"' not in raw:
    continue                      # from #12803: session_meta lines stop here
  ...
  if entry.get("type") == "session_meta":
    ...                           # from #12032: provider check, now unreachable
```

**Impact:** if both land, custom-provider rollouts count as Codex usage again, and the local ones are also counted by Local. With both test additions kept, #12032's provider test fails against the merged collector, so keeping both tests would catch it. **Suggested change:** whichever lands second should let `session_meta` lines through the prefilter.

Separately, open #10330 (pi) and #12635 (opencode) add collectors that count every provider, so they would also count the turns this tab counts. Whether overlapping tabs are intended is a maintainer decision.

**Optional test improvement:** three changes to the Local collector still pass all 11 assertions of the new test: removing the `scan.scan_pi()` call (there is no pi fixture), removing the `scanDate` check (the "another day" step adds no row between the cached and the fresh scan, so a hit and a miss both print 200), and removing the localhost, IP or bare-hostname rules (the only self-hosted URL fixture is `server.home`). A pi fixture including `llama.cpp`, a row inserted before the wrong-date check, a small `is_self_hosted` URL table and a no-`session_meta` rollout with a token-sum check in the partition test would cover these.

**Documentation:**
- README: "Every collector counts only the turns its own subscription paid for" does not hold for the Claude collector, whose `~/.claude/projects` scan has no provider filter. "Nothing a coding agent does goes uncounted" conflicts with the later note that third-party APIs are counted by no collector.
- README: ids "with no URL to resolve (…) fall back to" the runtime list, but the code checks the list first, so a Codex `vllm` provider configured with a public HTTPS `base_url` counts as Local.
- `manual/17-ai.md:39` still lists only Claude Code, Codex and Fireworks.

The #12803 interaction comes from a merge of both heads, run in the same sandbox, and source reading.
